questions.prompt: What happens when you compile this TypeScript snippet with strict: true?
options: Compile-time error: val is of type unknown
questions.explanation: TypeScript refuses property access on unknown until narrowed with typeof val === "string".

questions.prompt: Why does passing { x: 3, y: 4, z: 10 } stored in a variable satisfy a Point2D ({ x: number; y: number }) parameter?
options: TypeScript uses structural typing and the variable contains all required Point2D properties
TypeScript strips the z property at runtime
TypeScript ignores object properties on variables
questions.explanation: Structural typing allows any value whose shape contains at least the required members.

questions.prompt: Which TypeScript type accepts any value on assignment but forbids accessing properties until narrowed?
questions.explanation: unknown is TypeScript’s type-safe top type: safe to assign to, unsafe to use until narrowed.

questions.prompt: What happens when compiling this satisfies snippet?

codeSnippet.code:
const colors = { ok: '#10b981' } satisfies Record<string, string>;
const hex = colors.missing;

options: Compile-time error: Property "missing" does not exist
questions.explanation: satisfies retains the exact keys of colors ({ ok: string }), so accessing colors.missing fails at compile time.

questions.prompt: Which feature is supported by interface declarations but NOT by type aliases?
options: Declaration merging across multiple declarations with the same name
questions.explanation: Duplicate interface names merge automatically, whereas duplicate type aliases produce a compile error.

questions.prompt: What happens if a function parameter is typed as items: readonly string[] and you call items.push("x")?
options: TypeScript raises a compile-time error because push does not exist on readonly string[]
It silently returns a new array
It throws a TypeError only at runtime
questions.explanation: readonly string[] omits mutating methods like push, pop, and splice at compile time.

questions.prompt: What is the inferred type of result here?
questions.explanation: Overload resolution matches the second overload (x: number): number.

questions.prompt: Why does TypeScript allow passing `(x) => results.push(x)` (which returns a number) where a `(x: string) => void` callback is expected?
options: Contextual void indicates the caller ignores any returned value
TypeScript disables return checks on arrow functions
number is assignable to void everywhere
questions.explanation: void in a callback type means the caller ignores the return value, not that returning a value is illegal.

questions.prompt: Which signature does TypeScript use when checking a call to an overloaded function?
options: The first matching overload signature from top to bottom (never the implementation signature)
questions.explanation: TypeScript resolves overload calls top-down against public overload signatures only.

questions.prompt: Which directive reports a compile error if the next line actually compiles cleanly?
options: @ts-expect-error fails because no error occurred on the next line
questions.explanation: @ts-expect-error requires an error on the following line and flags unused suppressions.

questions.prompt: What type does `x` have inside the `if` block?

codeSnippet.code:
function isStr(v: unknown): v is string { return typeof v === 'string'; }
function run(x: number | string) { if (isStr(x)) { /* here */ } }

questions.explanation: The user-defined type predicate narrows x to string inside the true branch.

questions.prompt: After checking `if (typeof x === "string") return;`, what type does x have if it started as `string | number | boolean`?
questions.explanation: Control-flow analysis eliminates string from the union after the early return.

questions.prompt: What property enables TypeScript to narrow `{ ok: true; data: number } | { ok: false; error: string }` in a single `if (res.ok)` check?
questions.explanation: Literal tags like `ok: true` vs `ok: false` act as discriminants for automatic union narrowing.

questions.prompt: What is the return type of `getProp({ id: 1, title: "TS" }, "title")`?

codeSnippet.code:
function getProp<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K] { return obj[key]; }
const v = getProp({ id: 1, title: 'TS' }, 'title');

questions.explanation: K is inferred as "title", so T[K] resolves directly to string.

questions.prompt: What type is inferred for `res` when calling `function wrap<T>(v: T) { return { value: v }; } const res = wrap("TS");`?
questions.explanation: TypeScript infers T = string from the argument and substitutes it into the return shape.

questions.prompt: Given `interface Book { title: string; pages: number }`, what is the type `Book["pages"]`?
questions.explanation: Indexed access `Book["pages"]` looks up the exact property type (`number`).

questions.prompt: What type does `Exclude<"a" | "b" | "c", "a" | "c">` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Exclude removes "a" and "c" from the union, leaving only "b".

questions.prompt: Which utility type produces a version of `User` where `id` cannot be supplied and all remaining fields are optional?
questions.explanation: Omit removes `id`, and Partial makes all remaining properties optional.

questions.prompt: Why can `Pick<User, "id" | "name">` be safer than `Omit<User, "passwordHash">` for a public API response type?
options: If a new sensitive field is later added to User, Pick won’t accidentally expose it
questions.explanation: Allowlist selection (Pick) prevents newly added internal properties from leaking automatically.

questions.prompt: What type does `const [items, setItems] = useState([])` infer for `items` with strict: true?
questions.explanation: Without a generic argument, an empty array literal infers never[] in strict mode.

questions.prompt: What does `type Out = (string | number) extends string ? 1 : 0` evaluate to?
options: 0 (no distribution without a naked type parameter)
questions.explanation: Distribution only happens on naked generic type parameters, not concrete unions.

questions.prompt: What does `type IsString<T> = T extends string ? "yes" : "no"; type R = IsString<42>;` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: 42 does not extend string, so the false branch ("no") is chosen.

questions.prompt: What does `type Box<T> = T extends any ? { v: T } : never; type R = Box<string | number>;` resolve to?
questions.explanation: Because T is a naked type parameter, Box distributes over the union into `{ v: string } | { v: number }`.

questions.prompt: What type does `` type EventName = `on${Capitalize<"load" | "save">}` `` resolve to?
questions.explanation: Capitalize uppercases the first character of each union member cleanly.

questions.topic: Mapped Types, Key Remapping & Template Literal Types
questions.prompt: What does `{ [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] }` implement?
questions.explanation: Removing the optional modifier (`-?`) from every property of T is the exact definition of Required<T>.

questions.topic: Mapped Types, Key Remapping & Template Literal Types
questions.prompt: In `{ [K in keyof T as T[K] extends string ? K : never]: T[K] }`, what happens to properties whose value type is `number`?
options: They are excluded completely from the resulting type
questions.explanation: Remapping a key to `never` inside an `as` clause omits that property from the mapped type.

questions.prompt: What happens when you compile this strict type test?

codeSnippet.code:
type Expect<T extends true> = T;
type Check = Expect<false>;

options: Compile-time error: Type "false" does not satisfy constraint "true"
questions.explanation: Expect<T extends true> turns a failing type-level test into an immediate compile error.

questions.topic: Runtime Boundary Validation & End-to-End Type Safety
questions.prompt: Why does TypeScript NOT prevent a runtime crash if an external REST API unexpectedly returns `price: "free"` instead of a number?
options: TypeScript types are erased at compile time and do not inspect live network payloads
questions.explanation: Static types verify source code at build time; runtime boundary parsers are required for external data.

questions.topic: Runtime Boundary Validation & End-to-End Type Safety
questions.prompt: What advantage does returning `Result<User, "NOT_FOUND" | "UNAUTHORIZED">` have over throwing an Error?
options: The exact failure cases appear in the function’s static signature and callers must narrow `ok` before reading `value`
It executes without allocating any memory
questions.explanation: Result<T, E> encodes expected failure modes directly into the type system so callers cannot ignore them.

questions.prompt: In what order do `using a = res("A"); using b = res("B");` dispose when the block exits?
options: Both dispose concurrently in random order
questions.explanation: Explicit Resource Management disposes resources in reverse declaration order (LIFO).
